fact: A national program managed by the Rwanda Space Agency will use Planet's near-daily satellite data to monitor agriculture and food security, as announced by Planet and the Government of Rwanda.

The Rwanda Space Agency's GeoHub, supported by an AFD-backed project, uses satellite images to support sectors including agriculture, and geospatial data is already used to build climate projections informing agriculture and food security policy, per the interweave newsletter.
source_slug: 2024-09-30 Rwanda's digital transformation an effort at intergovernmental collaboration

fact: BMZ Digital.Global says the Rwanda Space Agency, the Ministry of Agriculture, Alliance Bioversity-CIAT and FAIR Forward developed a satellite and AI crop mapping method that is currently being tested in four districts for rice, maize, potatoes and beans.

fact: The Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT page says a GIZ-funded pilot, run with the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources and the Rwanda Space Agency from 15 November 2024 to 1 September 2025 in four districts, is developing an automated satellite-based crop mapping system to integrate with AMIS and SAS.

UK FCDO reports an active project, started 2024-11-08 and funded at GBP 43,000, in which the UK ONS supports Rwanda's national statistics institute NISR to bring Earth Observation techniques and machine learning into agricultural statistics.

fact: Cenfri says the Rwanda Space Agency processed three years of satellite images into weekly NDVI for just over 6,000 maize plots in a test of identifying underperforming fields; it calls the analysis a step needing refinement.

Digital Earth Africa reports a University of Rwanda graduate's research using Landsat NDVI from its platform, with climate data, to assess crop health in the drought-prone Rwimbogo sector, with field validation still to come.
